summary: At just 1.8 square miles with over 34,000 residents, Westmont packs roughly the population density of San Francisco into an unincorporated patch of south Los Angeles County — yet it appears on almost no one's mental map of the region. The landscape is flat and fully urbanized, part of the broad coastal plain between the Harbor Freeway and the 110, where the street grid runs unbroken and the built environment is dominated by single-family lots, apartment buildings, and strip-commercial corridors rather than any signature downtown or pedestrian core. The affordability math here is stark: a median home value around $617,300 against a median household income near $47,900 yields a price-to-income ratio above 12-to-1, making ownership a steep reach on local wages alone, while median rent of $1,413 consumes roughly 35 percent of that same median income. Employment skews toward the surrounding LA basin — healthcare systems, logistics hubs near LAX and the ports, and service-sector jobs — making this functionally a commuter area where the 110 and Metro bus lines carry workers outward. The climate is genuinely mild, averaging 74°F highs with over nine hours of daily sunshine year-round, so the weather rarely dictates plans. Westmont is a place where LA-basin proximity and moderate rents coexist with a housing-cost squeeze that the income data makes hard to ignore.
